1.competencias:
Reading and writing:
-Students will be able to read and understand short texts that includes-wh questions- (Who, What, When, Where, Why) to gather specific information about people, places, and objects, correctly using demonstratives ("this," "that," "these," "those") in their responses.
-Understand and create simple sentences and dialogues including formal and informal greetings while describing daily routines using the present simple and vocabulary seen. 
-To write short descriptions of objects and places using the present simple  and demonstratives ("this," "that," "these," "those"). They will also formulate wh questions to ask and answer for specific information. 

Speaking and listening: -To engage in conversations by asking and answering wh questions about people, places, and activities, using  demonstratives  ("this," "that," "these," "those") to provide and request specific information. They will practice asking questions such as "What is this?" or "Where are those items?" and respond appropriately to maintain a conversation.
-To improve the listening skills by understanding and responding to greetings(e.g., "Hello," "Good morning") and simple sentences that describe daily activities using the present simple tense. They will listen to conversations or instructions that include routine actions and respond to questions like "What do you do every day?" or "Where does he go after school?"
-Undestand and describe objects, people, and places using the present simple and demonstratives ("this," "that," "these," "those"). They will practice speaking tasks that involve describing where things are or what they are doing.
1.componentes:
Critical thinking -Today's children need to not only gain information, but to fully engage with it, process it and question it. Critical-thinking skills help children to do things such as determine facts, classify, order and prioritize information, make predictions and comparisons, reason logically and solve problems.
•        Communication- Language is, of course, all about communication. In order to communicate well, our children need to be able to listen, speak, read and write effectively. Bright Ideas offers students plenty of opportunities to develop these essential four skills. Oral practice of new language is paced carefully in controlled practice and freer practice stages, and throughout every unit.
•        Collaboration- Students who work together well not only achieve better results, but also gain a sense of team spirit and pride in the process. Bright Ideas encourages collaboration in every lesson, with students working together in pairs, small groups or as an entire class. In addition, the three student-centred projects after units 3, 6 and 8 of the course, as well as the Community Task at the end of Lesson 7 provide ideal scenarios for student collaboration. To participate in these activities, students need to learn to take turns, listen to others and acknowledge their contributions, and share credit for good ideas. 
•        Creativity- It is widely accepted that creative activities develop attention skills and promote emotional development.  Students who are able to exercise their creativity are also better at making changes and solving problems, they have learned not only to come up with new ideas, but to evaluate them and make choices.

Communicative skills:
Speaking: Describing outfits, styles, and colors; presenting fashion designs.
Writing: Creating short descriptions or scripts about clothing and accessories.
Reading: Texts, catalogs, or short articles about fashion, styles, and trends.
Listening: Fashion shows, model interviews, or videos describing clothes and styles.
4.evidencia_2:
Project: “Fashion Show: My Creative Design”
Objective:
To develop students’ ability to describe clothing, colors, and styles using the present progressive tense and adjectives.
To encourage creativity, confidence, and oral communication through fashion-related activities.
To promote teamwork and self-expression while integrating vocabulary and grammar in a fun, real-world context.
Main topics:
Present progressive (He/She is wearing…), clothing vocabulary, colors, adjectives for description (beautiful, elegant, sporty, casual), seasons, and materials.
Project: “My Fashion Show” – Oral Presentation or Runway Performance
Students will design and present their own fashion outfit inspired by a theme (e.g., seasons, professions, sports, or special events). 
During the show or presentation, each student will describe their design, including the clothes, colors, accessories, and style. 
The activity may include a short script, drawings, or a live modeling segment to make the presentation more engaging and creative.

Objective:
To develop students’ writing and speaking skills by representing a famous person from history.
To use the simple past tense (regular and irregular verbs) correctly in affirmative, negative, and interrogative sentences.
To encourage creativity, research, and expression through role-play and historical storytelling.

The episode should sound like a mini historical documentary or a movie-style narration, integrating storytelling and expressive voice acting.

1.evidencia_1:
Comunicative skills 

Speaking: Students will give short presentations comparing their daily routines and special activities, using the Present Simple and Present Continuous correctly. They will also talk about customs and traditions from different countries, explaining how people celebrate important dates.
Writing: In their notebooks, students will write short paragraphs about their daily habits and current activities, as well as brief descriptions of customs and traditions around the world. They will include dates and examples of how people celebrate them.
Listening: Students will listen to short interviews or watch videos about people’s routines, traditions, and cultural celebrations. They will identify when speakers use Present Simple or Present Continuous and take notes on key vocabulary.
Reading: Students will read short texts or articles about habits, celebrations, and traditions in different countries. They will answer comprehension questions, identify examples of Present Simple and Present Continuous, and create a small drawing or summary of what they learned.
1.evidencia_2:
Travel Diary
Objective:
To describe daily routines and family activities using the simple present tense.
To express personal experiences through creative writing and speaking activities.
To enhance creativity and teamwork through a shared project.
Main topics:
Daily routines, present simple, frequency adverbs, family activities, time expressions, and descriptive vocabulary.
Project:
“Travel Through My Day” – Creative Routine Diary
Students work in groups of four to create a shared diary. Each student takes the diary home in turns and writes about their daily routine, including school activities, meals, hobbies, and bedtime, as well as a short description of their parents’ routine. The diary should include drawings, decorations, and creative designs to make it visually appealing. Each entry must be dated and written in the first person. At the end, students will share their entries orally, describing what they do at home and what they learned from the experience.

Project: “Cultural Family Tree”

Objective:

To describe family members, traditions, and celebrations using possessive adjectives and the past simple tense.

To connect personal and cultural history through storytelling and written descriptions.

To use adverbial clauses and prepositions to express time, place, and relationships clearly.

Main topics:
Family vocabulary, possessive adjectives, past simple tense, adverbial clauses, prepositions of time and place, and cultural celebrations.

Project:
“Roots and Traditions” – Cultural Family Tree Presentation
Students will work in groups to create a visual “Cultural Family Tree.” Each student will choose a family member to research and include short written descriptions that tell stories, traditions, and personality traits. The project will feature historical references, photos, and creative visuals that represent their heritage. Students will use possessive adjectives and past tense forms accurately while describing relationships and events. Finally, each group will present their family tree orally, sharing how their family traditions connect to their culture.

Gerunds and infinitives (verb patterns and preferences), modal verbs (obligation, advice, possibility, necessity), I wish / If only structures, justice and injustice, betrayal, social inequality, human rights, ethical decision-making, and vocabulary for expressing opinions, emotions, and moral judgments.
Project Description: “International Forum for Justice and Restoration” – Debate and Proposal Presentation
Students represent different characters, groups, or social institutions inspired by The Count of Monte Cristo. Each group prepares a proposal addressing one of the key injustices or social conflicts present in the novel (e.g., wrongful imprisonment, corruption, abuse of power, revenge vs. justice, social inequality).

During the forum, students must:

Present their analysis of the issue based on the novel.

Propose ethical and realistic solutions to prevent similar injustices in modern society.

Use modal verbs to give advice and express obligation, and use I wish / If only to express regrets related to the characters’ decisions or outcomes in the story.

Debate with other groups, defending their proposals and responding respectfully using persuasive and formal language.

Final Product:
The project concludes with a collective “Declaration for Justice and Ethical Action,” written by the class. This document summarizes the most meaningful solutions discussed and connects them to the themes and moral lessons learned from The Count of Monte Cristo.

“The Media Fair” – Print Exhibition and Oral Presentation
Students create a printed media exhibit that showcases different text types —such as advertisements, short articles, and opinion pieces— about social communication, trends, or the influence of media on society.
Each group designs a display board or poster set, applying persuasive language, connectors, and correct grammar structures.
During the Media Fair, students present their work to classmates and visitors, explaining their messages and highlighting how language influences opinions and behaviors.

“My Life in Moments” – Personal Podcast or Digital Journal

Listening: Motivational talks and academic presentations
4.evidencia_2:
Project: “Unmasking Truth”
Objective
- To use future tenses, connectors, and persuasive language to discuss moral choices, consequences, and social judgment as presented in The Scarlet Letter.
- To develop critical thinking and oral communication through short, structured presentations.
- To encourage students to connect the novel’s themes with modern-day issues.
Main Topics: future tenses (simple, continuous, perfect), logical connectors, cause–effect connectors, persuasive expressions, public speaking strategies, moral dilemmas, social judgment, identity, and personal values.
Project: “Voices Behind the Letter” – Character Reflection Speeches
Students choose one main character from The Scarlet Letter (Hester, Dimmesdale, Chillingworth, or Pearl).
They prepare a short 4–6 minute speech as if they were the character, reflecting on:
- A decision they made
- How that decision affected their future
- What they wish they had done differently
- What they believe will happen next
- During the presentation, students must use future tenses, connectors, and persuasive sentences to justify the character’s actions and emotions.
- The project concludes with a brief class discussion comparing different interpretations of the characters and how their choices relate to social pressures today.
